column6: The original suggests a movement 'away from' trials, while the back-translation uses 'toward,' which alters the focus from escaping trials to moving towards a destination. Additionally, the phrase 'few have ever been in' is changed to 'only a few have ever gone,' which may imply a different nuance regarding the exclusivity of the destination.
column7: *Away from the trials that they are in,  \\\\nAway to a place of peace, love, and joy that few have ever been in.*
column8: "*away from the trials they are now in,  \\\\ntoward a place of peace, love, and joy where only a few have ever gone.*"

column6: The original uses 'away to' which implies a sense of movement or departure, while the back-translation uses 'toward,' which suggests direction rather than departure. This subtle shift can affect the interpretation of the journey to a place of divine ecstasy.
column7: *Away to a place of refreshing,  \\\\nto a place of Divine ecstasy.*
column8: "*toward a place of refreshing,  \\\\ntoward a place of divine ecstasy.*"

column6: The back-translated paragraph maintains the same conceptual meaning as the original, conveying the experience of a profound communication with the Lord while emphasizing the uncertainty of its audibility.
column7: There was one time when His Word came so clear and bold that it could have been audible. I answered Him by speaking out, it was so real. However, there was no one there but the Lord and I, so I can’t really say for sure if He spoke to me like we speak to each other.
column8: Once His word came so clearly and firmly that it might even have been audible. I answered Him out loud, because it felt so real. But there was no one there besides the Lord and me, so I cannot say for sure whether He actually spoke to me audibly, as we would speak to one another.

column6: The original emphasizes that 'KNOWING' is distinct from logic, while the back-translation suggests that understanding is formed through reasoning. This shifts the focus from a spiritual or intuitive aspect of knowing to a more cognitive process, altering the doctrinal implications.
column7: 2.  <u>The KNOWING is NOT built by logic within your mind; however, it is a complete thought or understanding.</u>
column8: 2.  <u>This understanding is not formed by the reasoning of your mind; yet it is a complete thought or perception.</u>

column6: The original uses 'convicts' and 'convinces,' which implies a distinction between guilt and persuasion, while the back-translation uses 'condemns' and 'assures,' altering the theological nuance of judgment and reassurance. This changes the understanding of how divine communication is perceived in terms of guilt versus encouragement.
column7: 5.  <u>When He speaks to His children, He NEVER CONVICTS; He CONVINCES.</u>
column8: 5.  <u>When He speaks to His children, He never condemns; He assures.</u>

column6: Both paragraphs convey the same theological message that God uplifts rather than belittles individuals, emphasizing the absence of doom and gloom in God's communication. The back-translation maintains the original intent and meaning while using slightly different wording.
column7: God never takes you down! He will never run you down; He only builds you up. When God speaks to you, He is speaking from the frame of reference that everything the Word says about you has already been accomplished and ACCEPTED by you. Jeremiah 33:3 says: “Call to Me, and I will answer you, and show you **GREAT AND MIGHTY** things which you do not know.” Does that sound like running you down or doom and gloom? There is NO doom and gloom in God, therefore He cannot tell you anything doomy or gloomy. You’ll have to tune in to the world’s news agency for doom and gloom.
column8: God will never take you down! He will never belittle you; He only builds you up/enlightens you. When God speaks to you, He speaks from the standpoint that everything the Word has said about you has already been accomplished and you have already received it. Jeremiah 33:3 says: “Call to Me, and I will answer you, and show you great and mighty things which you do not know.” Does that sound like He is belittling you or like destruction and darkness? There is no destruction and darkness in God, therefore He cannot say such destructive or depressing things. For destruction and darkness you must tune in to the world’s news agencies.
